-- Purpose: Consolidate small files without changing the sort order.

  table => 'compaction_bench.clean',
  strategy => 'binpack',
  options => map('rewrite-all','true',

views.dataset:
DATASET AND FILE LAYOUT

Deterministic synthetic events (not TPC-H / TPC-DS).
16,000,000 physical rows in 256 Parquet files; unpartitioned Iceberg v2.
1,267,756,086 data bytes = 1.18 GiB; average input file = 4.72 MiB.
Snappy compression; target output file size = 128 MiB (approximate).

Columns: id BIGINT, customer_id BIGINT, event_day DATE,
         amount DECIMAL(12,2), status STRING, payload STRING.
Customer IDs: 1 million possible values. Dates: 90 days.
Status: five values, with NULL on every eighth row.
Payload: a 64-character SHA-256 hex string, to avoid a trivial compressible dataset.

DELETE WORKLOAD
Five separate merge-on-read DELETE batches: pmod(id, 100) = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.
800,000 deleted rows (5%); 15,200,000 visible rows before AND after compaction.
256 position-delete files in the seed snapshot; no equality-delete workload.
The rewrite materializes deletes in the new data files. The 256 delete files
remain referenced in the resulting snapshot; delete-file cleanup is not measured.

WHY 10 FILES FOR BIN-PACK, BUT 9 FOR SORT?
Both engines produce the same file counts: 256 -> 10, or 256 -> 9 for sort.
Bin-pack groups whole input files into scan tasks; the final group is smaller.
Sort redistributes rows into 9 range partitions before writing.
128 MiB is a target, not a hard limit or a guarantee of exactly 10 files.
This reduces file count, not the logical data volume by 25 times.

GENERATOR SELECT (same values for clean and delete-seed tables)
SELECT id,
  pmod(xxhash64(id), 1000000) AS customer_id,
  date_add(DATE '2025-01-01', cast(pmod(id,90) AS int)) AS event_day,
  cast(pmod(id*37,100000)/100.0 AS decimal(12,2)) AS amount,
  CASE WHEN pmod(id,8)=0 THEN NULL
    ELSE concat('status_', cast(pmod(id,5) AS string)) END AS status,
  sha2(cast(id AS string),256) AS payload
FROM range(0,16000000,1,256);
views.machine:
MACHINE AND SOFTWARE

Mac16,7 | 14 logical CPUs | 48 GiB RAM | local filesystem
Spark local[8]: one machine, up to 8 concurrent Spark task threads.
Both arms: 4 GiB driver JVM heap + 8 GiB configured off-heap memory.
Spark 3.5.3 | Iceberg 1.8.1 | Comet 1.1.0-SNAPSHOT | Java 17.0.18 (Amazon)
Local development JAR; experimental native Iceberg writer enabled.
The JAR hashes identify the binaries. The working checkout had local edits;
its Git HEAD alone does not establish the exact source of these binaries.

CAPTURED COMET CONFIGURATION
spark.master=local[8]
spark.driver.memory=4g
spark.memory.offHeap.enabled=true
spark.memory.offHeap.size=8g
spark.sql.adaptive.enabled=false
spark.sql.shuffle.partitions=8
spark.plugins=org.apache.spark.CometPlugin
spark.sql.extensions=org.apache.iceberg.spark.extensions.IcebergSparkSessionExtensions,org.apache.comet.CometSparkSessionExtensions
spark.shuffle.manager=org.apache.spark.sql.comet.execution.shuffle.CometShuffleManager
spark.comet.enabled=true
spark.comet.exec.enabled=true
spark.comet.scan.icebergNative.enabled=true
spark.comet.scan.icebergNative.dataFileConcurrencyLimit=4
spark.comet.write.iceberg.splitOperator.enabled=true
spark.comet.iceberg.write.enabled=true
spark.comet.explain.planOnly.enabled=false

The JVM arm has Comet disabled and uses Iceberg's JVM reader/writer.
The SQL default is 8 shuffle partitions; the sort action requests 9 explicitly.
Flag names above belong to the measured local build.

views.method:
MEASUREMENT METHOD

5 paired rounds; separate JVM and Comet applications (10 applications total).
Engine order alternates by round. Each application runs bin-pack, deletes, sort.
One full warm-up rewrite immediately precedes each measured case in each app.
30 measured rewrites + 30 warm-ups. Results show medians, with JVM / Comet ratios.
The original seed snapshot is restored before every warm-up and measured trial.
The input file-manifest hash is checked each time; both arms read identical files.

Timer: time.perf_counter() around spark.sql(CALL ...).collect().
Includes procedure planning, data rewrite, and Iceberg snapshot commit.
Excludes Spark startup, data preparation, validation, plan export and seed restore.
A JVM checksum scan precedes every timed call: the filesystem cache is warm.
No Spark persisted data. One concurrent file group; partial progress disabled.

VALIDATION AND PLANS
All 60 rewrites matched row count, sum(amount), and two aggregate xxhash64 sums.
The two hashes cover all six columns and are summed as DECIMAL(38,0).
Clean cases preserve 16M visible rows; the delete case preserves 15.2M visible rows.
Comet output Parquet footers identify "Apache Iceberg 1.8.1 (Comet)".
Saved internal rewrite plans show native scan + native write in every Comet run;
sort also shows CometExchange (CometNativeShuffle) + CometSort.
The plan tabs show each engine's median trial, not necessarily the same round.
Read operator trees from the leaf scan upward. The outer CALL alone hides this work.
Local warehouse paths are shortened in the saved plans; operators are unchanged.

SCOPE
One machine, local storage, warm cache, synthetic data; no production guarantee.
No post-compaction read-latency, cold-cache, object-store or monetary-cost result.
No Z-order, equality-delete, delete-file rewrite or metadata-maintenance benchmark.
Native task CPU is not fully represented by Spark's task-thread CPU counter.

MEASURED SECONDS (rounds 1 to 5)

Bin-pack
  JVM   4.079, 3.877, 3.615, 3.651, 3.574 | median 3.651
  COMET 1.445, 1.659, 1.443, 1.338, 1.448 | median 1.445

Bin-pack + deletes
  JVM   4.438, 4.295, 3.982, 4.211, 4.600 | median 4.295
  COMET 1.930, 1.809, 1.353, 1.509, 1.273 | median 1.509

Sort compaction

  COMET 5.363, 4.817, 3.620, 4.156, 3.338 | median 4.156
